To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

personality traits are important predictors of career success, and that the Big Five personality traits are important determinants of career advancement, job satisfaction, and income across the life span.

conscientiousness and general mental ability were positively related to intrinsic career success, conscientiousness, neuroticism, and general mentalability were positively related to extrinsic career success (income and status), and personality was related to career outcomes controlling for general mentalability.

conscientiousness and general mental ability were positively associated with both intrinsic and extrinsic success, neuroticness was negatively associated with extrinsic success, agreeableness was negatively associated with intrinsic success, and openness was positively associated with intrinsic success.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question, "What personality traits are associated with career success?
the role of dispositional factors in career success, with a particular focus on personality and mental ability.
the extent to which personality is related to career success, and whether personality traits are associated with career success above and beyond the effects of general mental ability.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
personality is a relatively unexamined antecedent of career success.
personality and general mental ability are important predictors of career success.
the Big Five personality traits are related to career success, but that the nature and extent of the relationships are not yet fully understood.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
personality traits and general mental ability are related to career success.
the Big Five personality traits, and general mental abilities, are important influences on career success across the life span, and these effects are largely independent of each other.
the personality traits of conscientiousness and neuroticism are important determinants of both extrinsic and intrinsic career success.
The main takeaway from our work is that
personality is related to career success.
the Big Five and general mental ability are important determinants of career outcomes.
personality and general mental ability have important effects on career success, both directly and indirectly, and that these effects are not trivial.
